wallers-baptist-partlow.assessment: Wallers Baptist Church holds a remarkable distinction: founded in 1769, it claims the title of longest continuously operating Baptist church in the Commonwealth of Virginia — predating the Revolutionary War and the United States itself. That kind of institutional longevity in a rural Spotsylvania County setting speaks to deep community roots and theological stability. The church self-describes with three pillars — 'Bible-believing, Jesus-teaching, and people-loving' — which is clean evangelical language. FaithStreet confirms SBC affiliation, giving a solid denominational foundation on inerrancy, complementarianism, and soteriology. 'Pastor Patrick' is Moop's friend, which is the relational glue that makes this worth visiting. BGAV directory lists a different pastor name (Rev. John Shutlock), which may reflect an outdated directory or a recent pastoral transition to Pastor Patrick. The traditional service format and rural context suggest a conservative, no-frills congregation. No dedicated men's ministry found, but Moop's existing relationship makes this a personal as much as a theological connection.

score_notes.christology: Self-describes as 'Bible-believing, Jesus-teaching, and people-loving church.' SBC heritage affirms Christ as the only Savior.
score_notes.scripture: SBC (FaithStreet confirmed) means adherence to Baptist Faith & Message 2000, which affirms full inerrancy and Scripture as final authority.
score_notes.gender: FaithStreet confirms SBC affiliation. Baptist Faith & Message 2000 requires male-only pastoral leadership and affirms biblical manhood and womanhood. Traditional service culture reinforces conservative gender theology.
score_notes.leadership: Pastor Patrick leads; no elder board structure confirmed publicly. Traditional Baptist deacon model likely. BGAV directory discrepancy with website pastor name warrants direct confirmation.
score_notes.soteriology: Baptist/SBC means faith alone is the baseline. 'Jesus-teaching' language reinforces gospel centrality.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT language found; community outreach ministry is service-focused. Rural Spotsylvania County church — low exposure to progressive institutional pressure.
score_notes.preaching: Traditional service style; preaching content and expository vs. topical approach unknown.
score_notes.mission: Community outreach mission ('being the hands and feet of Jesus to our community and the world') plus 'Bible-believing' core identity reflects healthy evangelical mission posture.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: No standalone men's ministry found; programs include youth group and community service.
score_notes.denominational: R63 re-validation: live homepage reachable. Site identifies as 'Baptist' and 'Bible-believing, Jesus-teaching, and people-loving'; founded 1769 (longest continually running Baptist church in VA); welcomes 'people of all ages, races, and backgrounds' (community-warmth, not affirming-sexuality language). No SBC or BGAV explicit statement on homepage this round; pastor name still not published on visible homepage. No women pastors, no CBF 'freedoms' rhetoric, no affirming language detected. Prior FaithStreet SBC + BGAV directory dual-alignment unchanged. Held YELLOW pending direct confirmation of pastor identity and BFM2000/men's-ministry evidence.

washington-community-fellowship.assessment: Washington Community Fellowship is a long-standing evangelical congregation in NE Washington, DC (Capitol Hill area) with Mennonite/Anabaptist roots, describing itself as 'Christ-centered' and called to personal transformation, authentic community, and social impact. The Anabaptist tradition (Mennonite, Brethren) is one of the historic Reformation streams, historically emphasizing discipleship, community, peacemaking, and radical following of Jesus. Strengths: genuine community emphasis, NE DC neighborhood engagement, ecumenical but Christ-centered orientation. Cautions: Anabaptist traditions vary widely on Scripture's authority and gender roles; many Mennonite-affiliated churches have moved toward egalitarian and progressive positions. Review their current statement of faith, pastoral authority structure, and specific positions on gender and sexuality. A community-focused church with historic roots — warrants direct investigation.

washington-national-cathedral.assessment: Washington National Cathedral is an architectural masterpiece and a significant national landmark — but from a USMC Ministries theological alignment standpoint, it is firmly not recommended. The Episcopal Church (TEC) has abandoned biblical authority on human sexuality, ordains women as bishops and priests, performs same-sex marriages, and its leadership uses the pulpit for progressive political advocacy. Bishop Mariann Budde's nationally publicized January 2025 inaugural sermon was a political statement, not a Gospel proclamation. The Cathedral has hosted interfaith services including Islamic prayers. The beauty of the building and the grandeur of the liturgy should not be confused with theological fidelity. This is included in the directory for situational awareness — military and government personnel in DC will be invited to events here. Know what you're walking into.

score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's discipleship ministry identified.
score_notes.denominational: Episcopal Church (TEC) is institutionally apostate — departed from biblical authority on sexuality, gender, and marriage.
score_notes.soteriology: TEC cathedral with 'A House of Prayer For All People' identity; emphasizes 'every person is a beloved child of God' — universalist-friendly framing. No substitutionary atonement or sola fide language. Black on TEC liberal trajectory.
score_notes.preaching: Lectionary-based liturgical preaching; 'Crossroads Podcast' and 'A Better Way' initiative suggest contemporary-social-issues orientation. Bishop Mariann Budde publicly preached against Trump administration policies in Jan 2025. Topical/social preaching pattern.

waypoint-church-colorado-springs-co.assessment: Waypoint Church is an Acts 29 + PCA dual-affiliated church plant in Colorado Springs, founded in 2021. Lead Pastor Steve Stanton shepherds the congregation around three movements: rest in God's love, restoration of wholeness through Christ, and work toward flourishing of neighborhoods, city, and nations. Strong dual-affiliation guardrails.
